name: Pasta with Cherry Tomatoes and Basil
pitch: With just your pasta, tomatoes, and basil already on hand, this simple Italian-style dish basically makes itself — a few pantry spices do all the heavy lifting.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook your pasta until al dente according to the package. Any pasta shape you have works great here.

While the pasta cooks, warm a generous splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add a pinch of garlic powder (or mince a fresh garlic clove if you have one) and let it sizzle for about 30 seconds.
If you have any sun-dried tomatoes tucked away, toss them in now and stir for 2 minutes — totally fine to skip them if not.

Add your fresh tomatoes (halved if they're cherry-sized, roughly chopped if larger), a pinch of chili flakes if you like a little heat, and a pinch of dried oregano. Cover and cook for 10–15 minutes until the tomatoes break down into a saucy, jammy situation.
Tear in your fresh basil and season with salt to taste.
Drain the pasta and toss it straight into the pan with the sauce. Stir everything together over low heat for a minute or two so the pasta soaks up all that flavor.
Serve as-is, or with a little grated parmesan or pecorino on top if you have it.

name: Baked Tomato Spaghetti
pitch: If you have a little extra time, roasting your tomatoes in the oven turns this three-ingredient pantry dinner into something that tastes way more special than the effort involved.
steps: Halve your tomatoes and spread them in a single layer in a baking dish. Tuck in your fresh basil leaves, drizzle everything generously with olive oil, and season well with salt and pepper. No thyme? No problem — the basil carries it beautifully on its own.
Roast for about 40–45 minutes until the tomatoes are soft, jammy, and just starting to caramelize at the edges. That's where the flavor is.
About 10 minutes before the tomatoes are done, cook and drain your spaghetti (or whatever pasta you have) according to the package.
Add the drained pasta straight into the baking dish with the tomatoes and toss everything together well, scraping up all the good bits from the bottom.
Serve right away — maybe with a drizzle of fresh olive oil over the top.

name: Tomato Pasta with Shrimp (or without!)
pitch: The tomato-basil sauce here is genuinely delicious on its own over pasta — the shrimp and scallops are a nice bonus if you happen to have them, but honestly don't stress it.
steps: If you have shrimp or scallops, season them with salt and pepper and set aside. If not, no worries — you're making a great tomato pasta.
Warm a generous splash of olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat. If cooking shrimp, add them now and cook about 2–3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Set aside in a bowl.
In the same pan, add a little more oil and a clove of minced garlic (or a pinch of garlic powder) and cook for about a minute until golden and fragrant.
Add your tomatoes — canned, fresh, or both — plus about 1 cup of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it turns into a proper sauce.
While the sauce simmers, cook your pasta in a separate pot of salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Stir any fresh tomatoes and your shrimp (if using) back into the sauce off the heat. Toss in the pasta, scatter over the fresh basil, and serve.
